title: Processing of identified data
description: The grading service processes student identification data (student ID) as part of the assignment submission process.
assumptions: Student ID is collected and processed as part of the assignment submission workflow.

title: Identifier in submitted data
description: Student ID is included in the assignment file submission, which contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier for the student within the system.

title: Attributable data evidence
description: The assignment submission with student ID and submission time can be attributed to a specific student, preventing them from denying the submission.
assumptions: The submission is recorded with student ID and timestamp.

title: Linking through unique identifier
description: Student ID stored in the assignment store can be used to link assignment data with other student records across different systems or databases.
assumptions: Student ID is used as a unique identifier that may be shared across systems.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Student ID and course information may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic assignment storage.
assumptions: The system may only need to store submission content, not necessarily student identifiers.

title: Unawareness of processing
description: Students may not be fully aware that their assignment submissions and associated metadata (student ID, course, submission time) are being stored and potentially used for linking or analysis.
assumptions: Students submit assignments without explicit awareness of all data processing implications.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing student ID, course, and submission time may exceed what is functionally needed for the assignment storage functionality.
assumptions: The primary function is to store assignment files, and additional metadata may not be strictly required.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified data (teacher credentials and student submission data) during the login and queue retrieval process.
assumptions: Assumes the system processes identifiable information during normal operation

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Student submission data may include more sensitive data types than functionally required for the teacher to review their course submissions.
assumptions: Assumes the system may disclose more sensitive data than necessary for the stated purpose

title: Amount
description: An excessive amount of personal data (student submissions) may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for the teacher to review their course submissions.
assumptions: Assumes the system may return more data than the teacher actually needs to review

title: Involved parties
description: Personal data (student submissions) may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., unauthorized access to submission queues).
assumptions: Assumes there may be security controls that could be bypassed

title: Processing of identified data
description: The teacher (ExternalEntity) provides identified information (login credentials) when logging into the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher provides identifiable information during login

title: Data
description: Login credentials can be used to prevent the teacher from denying certain claims about their access to the submission queue.
assumptions: Assumes login credentials are used for authentication

title: Excessive sensitive data collection
description: The grades portal may collect more sensitive data types than functionally required for the student to view their own grades and feedback.

title: Excessive data volume
description: The system may process more personal data than functionally needed for the student to view their own grades and feedback.

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Personal data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways not necessary to achieve the functionality of viewing grades and feedback.

title: Excessive data exposure
description: Personal data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the student to view their own grades and feedback.

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: The student may lack control to set preferences or consent in how their personal data is processed or collected beyond what is needed for viewing grades.

title: Lack of data subject control over access
description: The student may lack control in accessing the personal data that is being processed, potentially limiting their ability to view or manage their data.

title: Lack of data subject control over rectification
description: The student may lack control in rectifying incorrect data or removing personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of viewing grades and feedback.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for the different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking in the grades portal system.

title: Excessive data types disclosed
description: The portal may display more sensitive data types than functionally required for the student to view their own grades and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may include additional data beyond grades and feedback that is not strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain - depends on actual data types displayed by the portal.

title: Fine-grained data disclosure
description: Personal data disclosed may be of a more fine-grained level of granularity than needed for the student to view their own grades and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may display detailed breakdowns or additional metadata beyond what is functionally required.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain - depends on actual data granularity displayed.

title: Data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: The student's grades and feedback may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the portal's purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the data may be accessible to unauthorized parties or in unintended contexts.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain - depends on access controls and data sharing policies.

title: Parent-Child Account Linking
description: Parent account is linked to child account through identifier relationship, enabling linking of parent's identity to child's data
assumptions: Parent-child relationship is established through account linkage mechanism

title: Quasi-identifier Combining for Parent-Child Linking
description: System combines parent identifier with child identifier to establish parent-child relationship for grade access
assumptions: Parent and child accounts are linked through shared or related identifiers

title: Processing of Identified Child Data
description: Grades Portal processes identified data (child's grades) when parent requests access
assumptions: Child's grades are identifiable personal data

title: Identifier-Based Child Identification
description: Child's account serves as unique identifier for accessing their grades
assumptions: Child account is unique within the system

title: Sensitive Data Type Disclosure
description: Academic grades are sensitive personal data that may be perceived as highly sensitive
assumptions: Grades are considered sensitive personal data under applicable regulations

title: Excessive Volume of Data Processed
description: System may process more child data than functionally needed for grade access request
assumptions: Only specific grades should be accessed, not all child data

title: Unnecessary Data Treatment and Analysis
description: Child's grades may be analyzed or enriched beyond functional requirements for parent access
assumptions: System may perform additional analysis on grade data

title: Child Unawareness of Data Processing
description: Child data subject may not be aware their grades are being accessed by parent
assumptions: Child may not have visibility into parent's access to their data

title: Lack of Parent Control Over Data Processing
description: Parent may not have full control over how their child's data is processed and disclosed
assumptions: Parent consent mechanisms may be limited or unclear

title: Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: System may process more personal data than actually needed for parent grade access functionality
assumptions: Data minimization principle requires only necessary data to be processed

title: Sensitive data type disclosure
description: Child's grades, feedback, and submission history are disclosed to parents, which may be considered sensitive personal data that should only be shared when strictly required for the educational purpose.

title: Excessive party exposure
description: Personal data is made accessible to parents (external entity) which may be more parties than functionally necessary for the core educational functionality of the portal.

title: Revealing attributes disclosure
description: The combination of grades, feedback, and submission history contains revealing attributes that support the identification of the child data subject.

title: Quasi-identifier combining data
description: The combination of grades, feedback, and submission history can serve as quasi-identifiers that can be used to link the child to other data sources.

title: Unawareness of data disclosure
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their grades, feedback, and submission history are being disclosed to parents, which is a form of processing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (grades, feedback, submission history) is processed and disclosed than is actually needed for the functional goal of sharing academic progress with parents.
